sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section discusses the Gemara's derivation that the phrase "on that day" in the verse about entering the Sinai desert refers to Rosh Chodesh, and Tosafos' question about why a different gezeirah shavah was not used.

translations.translation: "In the third month of the children of Israel's going out from the land of Egypt, on that day they came to the Sinai desert."
And it is brought in the Gemara,
It is written here "on that day they came to the Sinai desert" and it is written there
"This month shall be for you the beginning of months,"
just as there it is Rosh Chodesh, so too here it is Rosh Chodesh.
And Tosafos questioned,
for in Tractate Pesachim
it is brought
(on the verse
"And Hashem spoke to Moshe in the Sinai desert in the second year... in the first month"),
it derives "desert" from "desert,"
it is written here "in the Sinai desert" and it is written there
"And Hashem spoke to Moshe in the Sinai desert, in the Tent of Meeting, on the first of the second month,"
just as there it is on Rosh Chodesh, so too here it is on Rosh Chodesh,
and since in the verse "in the third month" it also says "desert,"
why did it not derive here "desert" from "desert"?
And it needs to be understood,
for ostensibly,
the derivation from the gezeirah shavah of "this" "this" reveals that the explanation of "on that day" is Rosh Chodesh,
unlike if they had learned from the gezeirah shavah of "desert" from "desert"
[where the teaching is only that the matter stated in the verse
("they came to the Sinai desert")
was on Rosh Chodesh]
the explanation of "on that day" would not be understood
[And there is a further advantage in the gezeirah shavah of "this" "this" over the gezeirah shavah of "desert" from "desert,"
for "this month" its explanation is Rosh Chodesh,
unlike "Sinai desert" and "first of the month"
(Rosh Chodesh)
which are two separate matters],
and what is the reasoning of Tosafos that it should have derived "desert" from "desert"?

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that the essence of receiving the Torah is the power given to each Jew for their Torah study to be in a state of utter self-nullification, which is connected to the revelation of Kesser on Shavuos.

translations.translation: And this will be understood according to what is explained in Torah Ohr, the discourse beginning with the word "Zeh,"
that the essence
of receiving the Torah is as it is written
(at the beginning of the matter of the Giving of the Torah)
"And Elokim spoke all these words, saying,"
for the explanation of the word "saying" in this verse is that at the time of the Giving of the Torah, the power was given to every single Jew,
that his study of Torah
[all these words,
which also refers to the entire Torah]
would be in the manner of "to say,"
to repeat the matters that the Holy One, blessed is He, says,
as it is written
"My tongue will answer Your word,"
that the Torah is "Your word,"
that my tongue answers like one who answers after the speaker.
And this is the connection of the Giving of the Torah to the holiday of Shavuos,
for on Shavuos is the drawing down of Kesser
[and as is known
in the explanation of the verse
"You shall count fifty days,"
that on Shavuos the fiftieth gate of Binah is drawn down,
and the fiftieth gate is Kesser],
and this that at the Giving of the Torah the power was given that the Torah study of Israel would be in ultimate self-nullification,
that he has no independent existence at all and is only like one who answers after the caller,
is because at the Giving of the Torah the revelation of Kesser was drawn down.
